neighbours.label: ' in' right after a change noun used without an adjective ('the change in', 'a decrease in', 'the drop in')
fire: Engineers tracked the change in water level throughout the night.
Analysts blamed the decline in exports on the strong currency.
Farmers reported a drop in yields after the dry spring.
Each experiment recorded the shift in pH after the acid was added.
Doctors noticed a decrease in swelling within two days.
The graph shows the variation in rainfall across the region.
Investors welcomed the rise in share prices on Friday.
This reduction in noise made the office easier to work in.
quiet: Engineers stayed in the control room throughout the night.
Analysts blamed the currency for weak exports last year.
Farmers in the valley reported poor yields after the dry spring.
Each experiment was repeated in a clean flask after the acid was added.
Doctors noticed that the swelling went down within two days.
The graph shows the rainfall in each part of the region.
Investors who live in Europe welcomed the news on Friday.
This quieter office made it easier for the team to work.

notes: Card: ' in' x28 after 'increase/rise/change(s)' in scientific prose. Probe: 'the change in' 0.44, 'The drop in' 0.29, but 'a small rise in' 0.10 and 'a sharp increase in' only 0.07, so an adjective before the noun seems to weaken it; locative 'in' 0.02-0.03, 'increase of' 0.03.
